title: Agent Patterns
subtitle: Manager-worker, dispatcher, map-reduce, pipeline and blackboard topologies
throughline: One question, fanned out across coordinating Electric Agent entities and synthesized back into one answer.

chapters.title: Manager-Worker
chapters.blurb: A manager spawns optimist, pessimist and pragmatist workers, wakes as each finishes, then synthesizes one answer.

story.title: Manager-Worker
story.subtitle: Manager-worker, dispatcher, map-reduce, pipeline and blackboard topologies

steps.title: Manager-Worker
steps.narration: **Manager-Worker** — a parent agent spawns specialist children, waits for all to complete, and synthesizes their results. `registerManagerWorker(registry)`.
steps.say: Start with a question worth more than one opinion. The manager hands it to a team and waits.
steps.coverSubtitle: One question, three perspectives, one synthesized answer

steps.title: One question arrives
steps.narration: The **user** asks one question. It arrives at the **manager** entity defined by `registry.define('manager-worker', ...)`, which runs an agent on `claude-sonnet-4-6`.
steps.say: A user asks one hard question. It lands on the manager, a coordinating entity registered with register manager worker.

steps.title: analyze with perspectives
steps.narration: The manager configures `ctx.useAgent({ model: 'claude-sonnet-4-6', tools: [...ctx.electricTools, analyzeTool] })`. The handler-scoped tool `analyze_with_perspectives` drives the fan-out.
steps.say: The manager runs an agent with one special tool, analyze with perspectives. Calling it kicks off the whole fan out.

steps.title: Spawn three specialists
steps.narration: `ctx.spawn('worker', childId, { systemPrompt: perspective.systemPrompt, tools: ['read'] }, ...)` for each of the three perspectives — **optimist**, **pessimist**, **pragmatist**.
steps.say: The manager spawns three workers, an optimist, a pessimist, and a pragmatist. Each is the same worker entity, just given a different system prompt.

steps.title: Same question to all
steps.narration: Each child is spawned with `{ initialMessage: question, wake: { on: 'runFinished', includeResponse: true } }`. The manager sends the same question to all three and returns immediately.
steps.say: It sends the very same question to all three as their initial message, then returns right away without blocking.

steps.title: Track children in state
steps.narration: `children.insert({ key, url: child.entityUrl, kind, question })`. The `children` collection uses `managerChildSchema` with `primaryKey: 'key'`, so the manager can later observe and reuse each worker.
steps.say: Each spawned worker gets a row in the children collection, recording its key, its url, its kind, and the question. That is how the manager finds them again.

steps.title: Woken on run finished
steps.narration: On each `wake: { on: 'runFinished' }`, the manager reads `wake.payload.finished_child.response` and writes it back with `children.update(key, draft => { draft.output = finished.response })`.
steps.say: Now the manager waits. As each worker finishes its run, the manager is woken again, and it stores that worker's response into the children collection.

steps.title: Synthesize one answer
steps.narration: When every worker has reported, the manager runs the **reduce** step over `state.children`, synthesizing the optimist, pessimist and pragmatist outputs into one **answer** returned to the user.
steps.say: Once all three have reported in, the manager runs its synthesis step. It reduces three perspectives into one answer and hands it back to the user.

chapters.title: Dispatcher
chapters.blurb: A stateless router classifies an incoming message and routes it to the right specialist, then forwards the reply.

story.title: Dispatcher
story.subtitle: Manager-worker, dispatcher, map-reduce, pipeline and blackboard topologies

steps.title: Dispatcher
steps.narration: **Dispatcher** — a router agent that classifies an incoming message and dispatches it to the appropriate specialist agent type. `registerDispatcher(registry)`.
steps.say: Sometimes the question just needs the right expert. The dispatcher reads it and routes.
steps.coverSubtitle: Classify the question, route it to the right specialist

steps.title: A message arrives
steps.narration: The **user** sends a message. It arrives at the **dispatcher**, defined by `registry.define('dispatcher', ...)` running an agent on `claude-sonnet-4-6`.
steps.say: A message comes in from the user. It reaches the dispatcher, a router entity registered with register dispatcher.

steps.title: No local state
steps.narration: The dispatcher defines **no `state` collections**. It is *stateless* — it relies entirely on the wake mechanism to receive child completion events and forward output.
steps.say: The dispatcher keeps no state collections of its own. It is stateless, leaning entirely on the wake mechanism to learn when a child is done.

steps.title: Classify with dispatch
steps.narration: The LLM classifies the message and calls the **dispatch** tool with `type`, `systemPrompt`, and `task` — the entity type to spawn and the original message to forward.
steps.say: The agent classifies the message and calls its dispatch tool, choosing a type, a focused system prompt, and the original task to forward.

steps.title: Route to a specialist
steps.narration: `ctx.spawn(type, id, { systemPrompt }, { initialMessage: task, wake: { on: 'runFinished', includeResponse: true } })`. The tool returns immediately with a status message.
steps.say: The dispatch tool spawns the chosen specialist with the task as its initial message, then returns right away with a status note.

steps.title: Woken when it finishes
steps.narration: The specialist runs, and on `wake: { on: 'runFinished' }` the dispatcher is re-invoked — no blocking, just an async completion event carrying the response.
steps.say: When the specialist finishes its run, the dispatcher is re-invoked. There is no waiting in place, just a wake.

steps.title: Forward to the user
steps.narration: The dispatcher forwards the specialist's output to the **user**. Because it is stateless, all it does is *classify, route, and forward*.
steps.say: Finally the dispatcher forwards the specialist's output straight back to the user. It coordinated without ever holding the work itself.

chapters.title: Map-Reduce
chapters.blurb: map_chunks splits the input, fans out one worker per chunk in parallel, then reduces every result into one.

story.title: Map-Reduce
story.subtitle: Manager-worker, dispatcher, map-reduce, pipeline and blackboard topologies

steps.title: Map-Reduce
steps.narration: **Map-Reduce** — split input into chunks, process all in parallel with worker agents, then synthesize. `registerMapReduce(registry)`.
steps.say: When the input is too big for one pass, split it. Run every piece at once, then combine.
steps.coverSubtitle: Split the work, run it in parallel, reduce to one

steps.title: Large input arrives
steps.narration: A large input reaches the **map-reduce** orchestrator, defined by `registry.define('map-reduce', ...)` and running an agent on `claude-sonnet-4-6`.
steps.say: A large input arrives at the map reduce orchestrator, an entity registered with register map reduce.

steps.title: map_chunks splits it
steps.narration: The agent runs `ctx.useAgent({ tools: [...ctx.electricTools, createMapChunksTool(ctx)] })`. The **map_chunks** tool splits the input into chunks.
steps.say: The orchestrator calls its map chunks tool, which splits the input into separate chunks ready to process.

steps.title: Fan out in parallel
steps.narration: **Map phase** — for each chunk, `ctx.spawn('worker', id, { systemPrompt: task, tools: ['read'] }, { initialMessage: chunks[i], wake: { on: 'runFinished', includeResponse: true } })`. All workers run simultaneously.
steps.say: In the map phase it spawns one worker per chunk, all at once. Every worker runs in parallel, each with its own slice of the input as its initial message.

steps.title: Record each worker
steps.narration: `ctx.db.actions.children_insert({ row: { key: id, url: child.entityUrl, chunk: i } })`. The `children` collection tracks each chunk worker with `primaryKey: 'key'`.
steps.say: Each spawned worker is recorded in the children collection by its key, its url, and its chunk index.

steps.title: Woken as each finishes
steps.narration: The tool returns at once; the entity is re-invoked on each `wake: { on: 'runFinished' }`, reading `finished_child.response` until every chunk worker has reported.
steps.say: The orchestrator returns immediately, then is woken as each worker finishes, with that worker's output carried in the finished child response.

steps.title: Reduce to one result
steps.narration: When all workers report via wake events, the LLM **synthesizes** results — the *reduce* phase — collapsing every chunk output into one result for the user.
steps.say: Once all workers have reported in, the orchestrator synthesizes their outputs in the reduce phase, returning a single result to the user.

chapters.title: Pipeline
chapters.blurb: run_stage chains sequential worker stages; each stage's output becomes the next stage's input via state transitions.

story.title: Pipeline
story.subtitle: Manager-worker, dispatcher, map-reduce, pipeline and blackboard topologies

steps.title: Pipeline
steps.narration: **Pipeline** — sequential stages where each stage's output feeds into the next via state transitions. `registerPipeline(registry)`.
steps.say: Some work has to happen in order. One stage hands its output to the next, all the way down.
steps.coverSubtitle: One stage at a time, each output feeding the next

steps.title: Input enters the pipeline
steps.narration: The **user** sends initial input to the **pipeline**, defined by `registry.define('pipeline', ...)` and running an agent on `claude-sonnet-4-6` with the `run_stage` tool.
steps.say: An initial input arrives at the pipeline orchestrator, an entity registered with register pipeline.

steps.title: run_stage spawns stage one
steps.narration: The LLM calls **run_stage** with `instruction` and `input`. `ctx.spawn('worker', id, { systemPrompt: instruction, tools: ['read'] }, { initialMessage: input, wake: { on: 'runFinished', includeResponse: true } })`.
steps.say: The agent calls run stage with an instruction and the input. The tool spawns a worker, using the instruction as its system prompt and the input as its initial message.

steps.title: Record the stage
steps.narration: `ctx.db.actions.children_insert({ row: { key: id, url: child.entityUrl, stage: stageCount } })`. The `children` collection tracks every worker by stage.
steps.say: Each spawned worker is recorded in the children collection by its key, its url, and its stage number.

steps.title: Output feeds stage two
steps.narration: On `wake: { on: 'runFinished' }`, the wake carries `finished_child.response`. The LLM calls `run_stage` again with the *previous output* as the next stage's `input`.
steps.say: When stage one finishes, the pipeline wakes with its output in the finished child response. It calls run stage again, feeding that output as the next stage's input.

steps.title: And on to stage three
steps.narration: The pattern repeats: stage two's `finished_child.response` becomes stage three's `input`. The LLM drives the pipeline *one stage at a time* until all stages are done.
steps.say: Stage two finishes the same way, and its output flows into stage three. The same loop repeats one stage at a time until every stage is complete.

steps.title: Final stage returns
steps.narration: When the final stage completes, its output is the pipeline's result, returned to the **user**. Each stage transition carried the question forward.
steps.say: The last stage produces the finished result, and the pipeline returns it to the user. One question has flowed cleanly through every stage.

chapters.title: Blackboard and Observers
chapters.blurb: A moderator runs pro and con workers over shared state, and reactive observers wake on change to watch entities.

story.title: Blackboard and Observers
story.subtitle: Manager-worker, dispatcher, map-reduce, pipeline and blackboard topologies

steps.title: Blackboard and Observers
steps.narration: **Blackboard** — multiple agents coordinate through shared state. Plus **reactive observers** that watch entities and wake on change. `registerDebate(registry)`.
steps.say: Not every team passes messages. Some coordinate by writing to one shared board everyone can read.
steps.coverSubtitle: Coordinate through shared state; wake on change to watch

steps.title: Moderator makes the board
steps.narration: On `ctx.firstWake`, the **moderator** calls `ctx.mkdb('debate-...', debateSchema)`, then `ctx.observe(db(...))` to connect to the **shared state** — the blackboard.
steps.say: A debate moderator creates the shared state on its first wake, then connects to it. This shared board is the blackboard everyone will read and write.

steps.title: Spawn pro and con
steps.narration: The `start_debate` tool spawns **pro** and **con** workers with `sharedDb: { id: 'debate-...', schema: debateSchema }`, so both connect to the same blackboard.
steps.say: The start debate tool spawns two workers, a pro and a con, each connected to the very same shared state through their shared database argument.

steps.title: Workers write arguments
steps.narration: Pro and con write to the shared `arguments` collection via auto-generated `write_arguments` tools (`type: 'shared:argument'`), each row tagged with `side` and `round`.
steps.say: Each worker writes its arguments into the shared arguments collection, tagged with its side, pro or con, and the round. They coordinate purely through what they put on the board.

steps.title: Moderator reads the board
steps.narration: The `check_debate` tool reads `shared.arguments.toArray`. After the rounds, `end_debate` reads all arguments and transitions `idle → debating → ruling → done`.
steps.say: The moderator reads the board with its check debate tool, sees the current arguments, and once the rounds are done writes its final ruling.

steps.title: An observer wakes on change
steps.narration: A **monitor** calls `ctx.observe(entity(url), { wake: { on: 'change', collections: [...] } })`. It is woken whenever the observed entity has new activity and reports status changes.
steps.say: A separate monitor entity can watch the board too. It calls observe entity on a url with a wake on change condition, so it is woken whenever the watched collections get new activity.

steps.title: Ways to wire entities
steps.narration: Every pattern is built from the same parts: `ctx.spawn`, `ctx.observe(entity(url))`, `child.send`, and **wake** conditions — *runFinished* for completion, *change* for reactive observers.
steps.say: So that is the toolkit. Spawn workers and wake on run finished, route with a dispatcher, fan out and reduce, chain stages in a pipeline, or share a blackboard and observe on change. Different ways to wire the same entities together.
